'''Scott Turner''' (born '''Graham Morrison Turnbull'''; August 23, 1931 – February 9, 2009) was a Canadian composer, producer, musician, and publisher whose career in the music industry spanned over 50 years, composing songs with [[Buddy Holly]], [[Audie Murphy]], [[Herb Alpert]], [[John Marascalco]] and many others.<ref name="obituary">{{cite web | url=http://www.inmemoriam.ca/view-announcement-14148-graham-turnbull.html# | title=Graham Turnbull Obituary | access-date=May 17, 2013}}</ref>

==Life and career==

===Early life===
Turner was born in Sydney, Nova Scotia, Canada, to Allison and Evelyn ({{nee}} Peters) Turnbull.<ref name="obituary" /> At the age of 19, he qualified for the All Canadian Track Team, and would continue to compete for Canada from 1950 to 1956, winning two Canadian long jump championships and representing Canada in the long jump at the 1954 British Empire Games in Vancouver.<ref name= "WhosWho" /><ref name= "Nilsson Associate" /> In 1952, at the age of 21, he moved to the U.S. and enrolled in the [[University of Dubuque]], Iowa. He received a Bachelor of Arts and Science degree from the [[University of Dubuque]] in 1955.<ref name= "WhosWho">{{cite book|title=Who's Who in the South and Southwest|year=1980–81|publisher=Marquis Who's Who, Inc.|location=Chicago, IL|isbn=978-0837908175|pages=[https://archive.org/details/whoswhoinsouthso0000unse/page/764 764–765]|url-access=registration|url=https://archive.org/details/whoswhoinsouthso0000unse/page/764}}</ref> While recuperating from a serious sporting injury, Turner taught himself to play guitar—a skill that would soon change the course of his life.<ref name= "Nilsson Associate" /> Though he enrolled in a post graduate program at [[Texas Tech University]], [[Lubbock]] in 1956, he would not stay long. In 1956, Turner befriended [[Buddy Holly]], a young Lubbock musician who would soon achieve worldwide success. Like Holly, Turner left his studies to pursue music in 1957. Turner and Holly ultimately wrote thirteen songs together.<ref name= "Nilsson Associate" /> And, Holly was just the first of many up and coming singers that would be mentored by Turner over the course of his lifetime.<ref name= "Nilsson Associate">{{cite web|title=Known Associates: Scott Turner|url=https://fortheloveofharrynilsson.blogspot.com/2011/01/known-associates-scott-turner.html|publisher=For the love of Harry Nilsson|access-date=May 17, 2013}}</ref>

===Life in music===
In 1957, Turner wrote his first songs for his good friend Hal Goodson, also from Texas Tech. Goodson recorded two songs at Petty Studios in Clovis, NM – "Who's Gonna Be The Next One Honey" and "Later Baby". These were the first songs that [[J.I. Allison]] recorded, several months before recording "Peggy Sue" with [[Buddy Holly]].{{citation needed|date=November 2022}}

From 1957 to 1959, Turner was lead guitarist for [[Tommy Sands (entertainer)|Tommy Sands]] and his band The Raiders (a.k.a. The Sharks, which included pre-[[The Wrecking Crew (music)|Wrecking Crew]] drummer [[Hal Blaine]]). From 1960 to 1961, Turner was lead guitarist and musical director for [[Guy Mitchell]], and served in the same capacities for [[Eddie Fisher (singer)|Eddie Fisher]] from 1961 to 1963. In 1963, Turner joined [[A&M Records]] as a writer/producer.<ref name= "WhosWho" /><ref name= "Nilsson Associate" />

From there, he went on to be general manager of Central Songs publishing company in Hollywood, and eventually became executive producer of the country division of [[Liberty Records|Liberty/Imperial Records]] in Hollywood.<ref>{{cite web|title=Meet the Music Morsels Writers|url=http://www.serge.org/musicmorsels/meet.htm|access-date=May 19, 2013}}</ref> In 1968, [[Liberty Records]] was bought for $38 million by [[Transamerica Corporation]] (an insurance company) and combined with their other label [[United Artists Records]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Alvin Silas Bennett|url=http://www.encyclopediaofarkansas.net/encyclopedia/entry-detail.aspx?entryID=7366|publisher=The Central Arkansas Library System|access-date=May 20, 2013}}</ref> Following that merger, Turner was transferred to Nashville to take over the country division of the newly merged Liberty/Imperial/United Artists.<ref name= "WhosWho" />

After leaving the label, he served as an independent producer on several albums for [[Slim Whitman]], garnering Turner four U.K Gold Records, and produced recording sessions for artists such as (in alphabetical order) [[Bobby Bare]], [[Larry Butler (producer)|Larry Butler]], [[Jimmy Bryant]], [[Vicki Carr]], [[Johnny Carver (musician)|Johnny Carver]], [[Jimmy Clanton]], [[Roy Clark]], [[Rosemary Clooney]], [[Penny DeHaven]], [[Waylon Jennings]], [[Bobby Lewis]], [[Willie Nelson]], [[Harry Nilsson]], [[Bill Phillips (singer)|Bill Phillips]], [[Del Reeves]], [[Ray Sanders (singer)|Ray Sanders]], [[Mel Tillis]], [[Cliffie Stone]], and [[Jerry Wallace]], among others.<ref name= "Nilsson Associate" />

Turner also worked in both film and television. He had a number of songs included in movies (see Compositions section below for more details), and his television credits include serving as music director for "Christmas on the General Jackson" (which led to the release in 1988 of a soundtrack album of traditional Christmas songs produced and arranged by Turner and Ron Bledsoe, and performed by [[Mel Tillis]], [[Kathy Mattea]], [[Lynn Anderson]], [[Butch Baker]], [[Donna Fargo]], and [[David Lynn Jones]], among others<ref>{{cite web|title=Christmas on the General Jackson|url=http://www.allmusic.com/album/christmas-on-the-general-jackson-mw0000199861/credits|publisher=Rovi Corp|access-date=May 20, 2013}}</ref>), and to making appearances on ''[[The Perry Como Show]]'', ''[[The Milton Berle Show]]'', ''[[The Mike Douglas Show]]'', ''[[Entertainment Tonight]]'' and ''[[A Current Affair (U.S. TV series)|A Current Affair]]''.<ref name= "WhosWho" />

===Compositions===
Turner ultimately wrote over 400 songs, many of which were co-written with artists such as (in alphabetical order) [[Herb Alpert]], [[Mac Davis]], [[Buddy Holly]] (13 songs in total, during writing sessions in Lubbock in 1957 and in New York in 1958), [[Mac Davis]], [[Diane Lampert]], [[Alex Harvey (musician)|Alex Harvey]], [[Red Lane]], [[John Marascalco]], [[Guy Mitchell]], [[Audie Murphy]] (83 songs in total), [[Harry Nilsson]] while at A&M, [[Johnny O'Keefe]], [[Doc Pomus]], [[Tommy Sands (entertainer)|Tommy Sands]], and [[Charles Williams (artist)|Charlie Williams]].<ref name= "WhosWho" />

Turner's songs have been recorded by (in alphabetical order) [[Kay Adams (singer)|Kay Adams]], [[Herb Alpert & the Tijuana Brass]], [[Eddy Arnold]], [[The Baja Marimba Band]], [[James Burton]], [[Larry Butler (producer)|Larry Butler]], [[Jimmy Bryant]], [[Roy Clark]], [[Jimmy Dean]], [[Penny DeHaven]], [[The Del-Vikings]], [[Dave Dudley]], [[Tennessee Ernie Ford]], [[Robert Gordon (musician)|Robert Gordon]], [[Bonnie Guitar]], [[Wanda Jackson]], [[Dean Martin]], [[Skeets McDonald]], [[Harry Nilsson|Nilsson]], [[Charley Pride]], [[Del Reeves]], [[Jean Shepard]], [[Wynn Stewart]], [[Sonny Throckmorton]], [[Gene Vincent]], [[Porter Wagoner]], [[Jerry Wallace]], [[Slim Whitman]], and [[Tammy Wynette]].<ref name= "WhosWho" /><ref name= "Turner Discography">{{cite web|title=Scott Turner discography|url=http://www.allmusic.com/artist/scott-turner-mn0000836599|publisher=Rovi Corp|access-date=May 20, 2013}}</ref>

Turner provided background tracks for a number of films, and three of Turner's songs were featured in the television movie ''[[Shout! The Story of Johnny O'Keefe]]''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Shout! The Story of Johnny O'Keefe|url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0090016/fullcredits?ref_=tt_cl_sm#cast|publisher=IMDb.com|access-date=May 19, 2013}}</ref> [[Herb Alpert]]'s 1964 recording of Turner's song "Mexican Drummer Man" was used in the 1966 [[Teri Garr]] short ''[[Where's the Bus]]'',<ref name= "Scott Turner IMDb">{{cite web|title=Scott Turner IMDb| website=[[IMDb]] |url=https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1321886/?ref_=ttsnd_snd_5|access-date=May 19, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Where's the Bus?| website=[[YouTube]] | date=May 13, 2011 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z396cRJiRdI|access-date=May 19, 2013}}</ref>  "One More River to Cross" (co-written with [[Freddie Scott]])<ref>{{cite web|title=One More River to Cross|url=http://repertoire.bmi.com/title.asp?blnWriter=True&blnPublisher=True&blnArtist=True&keyID=1122880&ShowNbr=0&ShowSeqNbr=0&querytype=WorkID|publisher=BMI|access-date=May 19, 2013}}</ref> can be heard in the [[Christopher Walken]] film ''[[The Opportunists]]'',<ref name= "Scott Turner IMDb" /> and "Little Pink Mack" (co-written with Chris Darrell Roberts and Jim Thornton)<ref>{{cite web|title=Little Pink Mack|url=http://repertoire.bmi.com/title.asp?blnWriter=True&blnPublisher=True&blnArtist=True&keyID=882373&ShowNbr=0&ShowSeqNbr=0&querytype=WorkID|publisher=BMI|access-date=May 19, 2013}}</ref> was used in the film ''[[Truckers]]''.<ref name= "Scott Turner IMDb" /><ref>{{cite web|title=Scott Turner CAE/IPI #: 31202352|url=http://repertoire.bmi.com/writer.asp?page=1&blnWriter=True&blnPublisher=True&blnArtist=True&fromrow=1&torow=25&affiliation=BMI&cae=31202352&keyID=350069&keyname=TURNER+SCOTT&querytype=WriterID|publisher=BMI|access-date=May 19, 2013}}</ref>

===Music publishing firms===
Publishing companies founded by Turner are Buried Treasure Music ([[ASCAP]]), Captain Kidd Music ([[Broadcast Music, Inc.|BMI]]), and Captain Kidd, LLC.<ref name= "WhosWho" /><ref>{{cite web|title=Buried Treasure Music|url=https://www.ascap.com/Home/ace-title-search/index.aspx|access-date=May 19, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Captain Kidd Music|url=http://repertoire.bmi.com/publisher.asp?blnWriter=True&blnPublisher=True&blnArtist=True&keyID=53061&keyname=CAPTAIN+KIDD+MUSIC&querytype=PubID|access-date=May 19, 2013}}</ref>

==Memorabilia==
Turner's memorabilia is now housed at the [[Willie Nelson and Friends General Store & Museum]], Nashville, Tennessee.<ref name= "WhosWho" /><ref>{{cite web|title=Willie Nelson and Friends General Store & Museum (Official Website)|url=http://www.willienelsongeneralstore.com/willie_nelson_store_history.html|access-date=May 19, 2013}}</ref>

===Biography===
As of June 2012, Australian biographer [[Damian Johnstone]] (author of "The Wild One: The Life and Times of [[Johnny O'Keefe]]" and 
"A Race to Remember: The [[Peter Norman]] Story"<ref>{{cite web|title=Damian Johnstone (author)|url=https://www.amazon.com/s/ref=ntt_athr_dp_sr_1?_encoding=UTF8&field-author=Damian%20Johnstone&search-alias=books&sort=relevancerank|publisher=Amazon|access-date=May 20, 2013}}</ref>) was writing a biography of Scott Turner with the working title "Shutters and Boards – The Scott Turner Story," which is tentatively planned for publication in 2013.<ref name= "Nilsson Associate" />
